title: Iran-Krieg: Golfstaaten bereiten sich auf neue Eskalation vor
content_c:
Iran-Krieg Golfstaaten bereiten sich auf neue Eskalation vor
Die Sorge vor einer erneuten Eskalation im Iran-Krieg wächst - vor allem in den Golfstaaten. Eine Folge: Aufrüstung. Auf einer Konferenz beraten Politiker aus der Region mit Experten. Auch Deutschland ist vertreten.
Gestörte Exportrouten für Öl- und Gas, fehlende Stabilität und wiederkehrende Angriffe: Die Diskussion in den arabischen Golfstaaten darüber, ob und wie sie ihre Geschäftsmodelle und Allianzen anpassen sollten, hat längst begonnen.
Auf der Sicherheitskonferenz Manama Dialogue drängt jedoch eine eiligere Frage in den Vordergrund: Planen die USA einen nächsten großen militärischen Schlag gegen Iran?
Neue US-Angriffe auf Iran nach den Zwischenwahlen?
Dass eine neue Phase der Eskalation bevorstehe, werde allgemein angenommen, sagt Hasan Alhasan. Er leitet beim Thinktank Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) die Forschungen zur Golfregion. Signale aus der Trump-Regierung deuteten darauf hin, dass Vorbereitungen im Gange sind. "Eine neue Runde der Kämpfe könnte unmittelbar bevorstehen."
Das könnte kurz nach den Zwischenwahlen in den USA am Dienstag sein. Alhasan betont jedoch auch: Unvermeidbar sei ein Wiederaufflammen des Konflikts nicht.
Iran-Krieg ist Schlag für die Wirtschaft
Alhasans Thinktank hat eingeladen zur großen Sicherheitskonferenz in Manama, der Hauptstadt des Inselkönigreichs Bahrain im Persischen Golf. Gekommen sind hochrangige Militärs sowie Außen- und Sicherheitspolitiker. Sie kommen aus der arabischen Welt, aus Asien, den USA und auch aus Deutschland, so auch Nils Schmid, SPD-Politiker und parlamentarischer Staatssekretär im Verteidigungsministerium.
Er betont: "Wir sind schon jetzt massiv von den Auswirkungen des Krieges hier in der Golfregion betroffen - durch steigende Ölpreise, durch steigende Inflation, durch die Schwächung der Weltwirtschaft." Laut Schmid würde ein erneutes Aufflammen des Kriegs auch erneut die Wirtschaft in Deutschland und Europa schwächen. "Deshalb setzen wir uns für eine diplomatische Lösung ein."
Doch was, wenn Appelle und diplomatische Vorstöße verhallen? Wenn Iran als Reaktion auf einen möglichen US-Angriff wieder massiv Energieanlagen und Militärbasen ins Visier nimmt?
Golfstaaten rüsten auf
"Ich glaube, wir sind gut vorbereitet auf das, was auf uns zukommt", sagt Mariam al-Dhain, Abgeordnete des Parlaments von Bahrain. Sie betont, wie besonnen die Führung ihres Landes sei: "Wir haben uns intensiv mit strategischen Überlegungen befasst, daher bin ich der Ansicht, dass Bahrain zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt sehr gut aufgestellt ist."
Mehr will, mehr darf sie wohl nicht sagen. Öffentliche Meinungsäußerungen werden in Bahrain streng kontrolliert. Konkreter wird Sascha Bruchmann. Auch der Militäranalyst arbeitet für den Thinktank IISS in Manama: "Wir sehen deutlich, dass die Golfstaaten eingekauft haben." Er nennt einen Deal mit der Ukraine über Drohnenabwehrtechnologie.
Außerdem hätten die Golfstaaten Milliarden in US-amerikanische Systeme gesteckt, trainiert und die eigenen Systeme und Strukturen überarbeitet. Bruchmann sagt, die USA würden für die Golfstaaten mittelfristig der mit Abstand wichtigste Partner in der Verteidigung bleiben.
Frustration über Trump
Gleichzeitig ist die Frustration darüber nicht zu überhören, dass US-Präsident Donald Trump den Krieg gegen Iran begonnen hat, obwohl die arabischen Golfstaaten davor gewarnt haben.
"Die Golfstaaten sind sich zweifellos darüber im Klaren, dass sie sich nicht auf Dauer auf die USA verlassen können", so Bruchmanns Kollege Hasan Alhasan. Die Folge sei die Entstehung neuer regionaler Sicherheitsbündnisse und -allianzen.
Er spricht das Verteidigungsbündnis zwischen Saudi-Arabien, der Türkei und Pakistan an. Auch andere Staaten in der Region seien dabei, sich neue, zusätzliche Partner für ihre Sicherheit zu suchen. Als Lieferant von Verteidigungssystemen spielt Südkorea eine immer größere Rolle. Die Vereinigten Arabischen Emirate setzen zudem auf israelische Technologie.
Griechenland für mehr Engagement der EU
Seltener fallen in Manama die Namen europäischer Staaten, wenn es um Sicherheit und Verteidigung geht. Dabei sind Vertreter aus der EU in Bahrain durchaus präsent.
Zur Eröffnung fordert der griechische Ministerpräsident Kyriakos Mitsotakis ein stärkeres europäisches Engagement für die Freiheit der Seewege, auch mit militärischen Mitteln: "Wenn uns die Sicherheitsanliegen unserer Freunde am Golf wirklich am Herzen liegen, müssen wir aktiver unter Beweis stellen, dass wir unseren Worten auch Taten folgen lassen."
Konkret spricht Mitsotakis die EU-Marine-Mission "Aspides" an, die das Ziel hat, internationale Handelsschiffe vor Angriffen der jemenitischen Huthi zu schützen. Derzeit beteiligen sich fünf EU-Staaten an "Aspides", unter ihnen Deutschland. Es könnten jedoch auch zehn sein, so der griechische Regierungschef.
Schmid setzt auf Diplomatie
Nils Schmid betont mehrfach, wie wichtig eine diplomatische Lösung sei. Die Europäer wollten sich für Gespräche einsetzen: "Nicht nur über einen Waffenstillstand und über eine Wiedereröffnung der Straße von Hormus" solle gesprochen werden. "Auch die tieferliegenden Probleme des iranischen Nuklearprogramms, des iranischen Raketenprogramms müssen in Gesprächen gelöst werden."
Vertreter Irans sind beim Manama Dialogue allerdings nicht anwesend. Als einziger arabischer Golfstaat pflegt Bahrain keine diplomatischen Beziehungen zur Regierung in Teheran. Gleichzeitig führen Delegierte aus dem Emirat Katar Gespräche mit der Regierung in Teheran, um zwischen Iran und den USA zu vermitteln - in der Hoffnung, dass es doch nicht zu der von vielen erwarteten Eskalation kommt.

title: У Луганську повідомляють про численні вибухи: під удар могла потрапити телефонна компанія
content_c:
У Луганську повідомляють про численні вибухи: під удар могла потрапити телефонна компанія
У тимчасово окупованому Луганську повідомляють про атаку безпілотників і можливе ураження місцевої телефонної компанії.
У тимчасово окупованому Луганську повідомляють про численні вибухи на тлі атаки БпЛА.
Про це пише Telegram-канал Exilenova+.
За попередньою інформацією каналу, під удар могла потрапити «Луганська телефонна компанія».
Даних про масштаби пошкоджень і можливих постраждалих наразі немає. Інформація про ураження компанії потребує підтвердження.
Нагадаємо, що раніше повідомлося, що в окупованому Луганську пролунали десятки вибухів: під ударом опинився центр зв'язку

title: Удар по многоэтажному дому в Харьковской области: среди 11 пострадавших — трехлетний ребенок
content_c:
Вечером 1 ноября российские оккупанты нанесли удар беспилотным летательным аппаратом по многоэтажному дому в поселке Васищево, расположенном в 20 км от Харькова. Об этом сообщил глава ОГА Олег Синегубов.
«Зафиксировано попадание в крышу пятиэтажного жилого дома. Повреждены два частных жилых дома. Локализован пожар в теплице площадью 20 кв. м», — уточнил Синегубов.
Он добавил, что среди пострадавших — 18-летний молодой человек и четыре женщины в возрасте 48, 67, 33 и 71 года.
Позже в Харьковской областной прокуратуре добавили, что число пострадавших возросло до 11.
«Пострадали 11 человек, среди которых — 3-летняя девочка. У большинства пострадавших диагностировали острую стрессовую реакцию», — сообщили в пресс-службе.
В прокуратуре предоставили больше подробностей. Как выяснилось, для атаки оккупанты применили БПЛА «Герань-3». В результате попадания загорелась крыша пятиэтажного дома.
Начато досудебное расследование по факту совершения военного преступления (ч. 1 ст. 438 УК Украины).
Ранее ZN.UA сообщало об атаке российских беспилотников на поселок Васищево 28 мая 2025 года, когда среди восьми пострадавших была четырехлетняя девочка.
В течение 1 ноября под российскими атаками находились также другие регионы Украины. В частности, в Киевской области зафиксировали повреждения жилых домов и энергетической инфраструктуры, а в Ровенской области в результате попадания дрона в дом пострадали четвыре человека.
description: В посёлке Васищево произошёл обстрел многоквартирного дома.

Вечером 1 ноября российские оккупанты нанесли удар беспилотным летательным аппаратом по многоэтажному дому в поселке Васищево, расположенном в 20 км от Харькова. Об этом сообщил глава ОГА Олег Синегубов.
«Зафиксировано попадание в крышу пятиэтажного жилого дома. Повреждены два частных жилых дома. Локализован пожар в теплице площадью 20 кв. м», — уточнил Синегубов.
Он добавил, что среди пострадавших — 18-летний молодой человек и четыре женщины в возрасте 48, 67, 33 и 71 года.
Позже в Харьковской областной прокуратуре добавили, что число пострадавших возросло до 11.
«Пострадали 11 человек, среди которых — 3-летняя девочка. У большинства пострадавших диагностировали острую стрессовую реакцию», — сообщили в пресс-службе.
В прокуратуре предоставили больше подробностей. Как выяснилось, для атаки оккупанты применили БПЛА «Герань-3». В результате попадания загорелась крыша пятиэтажного дома.
Начато досудебное расследование по факту совершения военного преступления (ч. 1 ст. 438 УК Украины).
Ранее ZN.UA сообщало об атаке российских беспилотников на поселок Васищево 28 мая 2025 года, когда среди восьми пострадавших была четырехлетняя девочка.
В течение 1 ноября под российскими атаками находились также другие регионы Украины. В частности, в Киевской области зафиксировали повреждения жилых домов и энергетической инфраструктуры, а в Ровенской области в результате попадания дрона в дом пострадали четвыре человека.

title: Гуманітарний режим тиші в Олешках завершився після доставки допомоги та евакуації цивільних – Лубінець
content_c:
Гуманітарний режим припинення вогню у тимчасово окупованому місті Олешки Херсонської області, який діяв із 27 жовтня за координації першої леді США Меланії Трамп, завершився у неділю після успішної доставки допомоги та евакуації мирних жителів, повідомив уповноважений Верховної Ради з прав людини Дмитро Лубінець у неділю.
"Режим тиші, який діяв із 27 жовтня до 1 листопада, завершився. Це був важливий етап спільної гуманітарної роботи разом із Уповноваженою з прав людини РФ Яною Лантратовою за координації Першої леді Сполучених Штатів Меланії Трамп. Протягом цього періоду сторони дотримувалися взятих на себе зобов'язань. Це дало можливість доставити гуманітарну допомогу до Олешок і допомогти цивільним мешканцям, які хотіли безпечно залишити місто", – написав омбудсман у телеграм-каналі.
За словами Лубінця, наразі українська сторона спільно з російською омбудсманкою опрацьовує можливості для продовження аналогічних гуманітарних заходів задля збереження дієвого механізму взаємодії та подальшого порятунку людей.
Як повідомлялося, з 3:00 вівторка, 27 жовтня, до неділі, 1 листопада, у визначеному районі тимчасово окупованих Олешків та прилеглих населених пунктів діяв режим припинення вогню за посередництва Ватикану та першої леді США Меланії Трамп. Раніше у неділю Трамп відзначила, що перемир'я забезпечило місцевим жителям доступ до продовольства, питної води, ліків і вільного пересування, та висловила сподівання, що Олешки стануть відправною точкою для тривалого миру.

title: Lindsay Clancy is back in court - where will her case go next?
content_c:
Lindsay Clancy is back in court - where will her case go next?
- Published
Lindsay Clancy, the US woman accused of murdering her three children, will return to a Massachusetts court on Monday as lawyers debate retrying the case.
Her defence team and Massachusetts prosecutors are expected to discuss how to move forward, with both parties seeking different outcomes.
Last week, in response to a defence request to dismiss the trial, prosecutors offered their clearest hint yet that they are seeking a new trial before a different jury. "The Commonwealth [Massachusetts] should be permitted to continue to pursue justice for Cora, Dawson and Callan Clancy," her three children, prosecutors said.
Prosecutors could also reduce the charges in a potential second trial or dismiss them altogether.
Clancy's first trial ended in a mistrial after a 12-person jury failed to reach a consensus.
The 36-year-old has not denied killing her children in 2023, but her defence team argues she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time. Prosecutors say the killings were intentional.
What happened when Clancy was last in court?
A jury first heard Clancy's case in August 2026, but failed to reach a unanimous agreement on whether the prosecution had proved Clancy was guilty "beyond a reasonable doubt" as required by US law.
A judge declared a mistrial in early September.
At a court appearance later that month, Clancy's lawyer, Kevin Reddington, argued the judge should dismiss her case. Meanwhile, prosecutors said the state had "met its burden" in proving her guilt.
But the hours-long back-and-forth ultimately didn't lead to a clearer answer about what might come next for Clancy - a dismissal of charges, retrial of the same charges, or retrial of lesser charges. These discussions will resume on Monday.
Judge William Sullivan seemed confident the case would be retried, saying in September he wanted to "get this thing moving".
He asked both sides to prepare to discuss possible trial dates at the November hearing.
Reddington said he would be unable to go to trial until at least June 2027 if the case was retried.
District Attorney Timothy Cruz said at the time that prosecutors had not yet decided whether to retry Clancy.
"We're doing our due diligence; we're going to continue doing that," he said. "We're going to do what we can for the children. That's what this case is about."
What do Clancy's legal team want?
Fundamentally, Clancy's legal team - with Reddington at the helm - is pushing for the charges to be dismissed or dropped. They've explored a variety of legal avenues.
In September, he asked for her to be found not guilty under Rule 25 - a Massachusetts provision that states a defendant should be found not guilty if prosecutors do not present enough evidence at trial.
That request was denied.
Judge Sullivan will hear arguments on several motions on Monday, but Heather Cucolo, a New York Law School professor and mental health law expert, told the BBC that the hearing will likely focus on a narrow point: was this an instance of a routine deadlocked-jury mistrial - in which the jury genuinely could not agree - or was this an improperly terminated trial?
She said Reddington may argue that a retrial could violate Clancy's Constitutional protection against double jeopardy - a legal standard that says a person cannot be tried for the same crime twice.
But legal experts agree that outcome is unlikely.
"The public attention that's been put on this trial and the need to have some conclusion in the near future, I think that the judge is going to say that this mistrial was appropriate, was legally accurate, and that they need to now look to set a date for a retrial," Cucolo said.
What do prosecutors want?
While the state's legal team has not explicitly said they will pursue a retrial, Cruz and the prosecutors who argued the case have consistently said they want justice for Clancy's children.
Last week, prosecutors asked Judge Sullivan to reject the motion to dismiss charges against Clancy on the grounds of double jeopardy.
They argue mistrial procedures were properly followed by the court, and thus they have a right to seek justice again on behalf of the children.
"Because a mistrial was properly declared due to the manifest necessity of a deadlocked jury, the defendant's motion to dismiss should be denied," prosecutors wrote in the motion.
What could happen on 2 November?
Judge Sullivan could make a determination over whether the case can proceed on Monday or he could rule later in writing, criminal defence lawyer Elyse Hershon told the BBC.
And how the District Attorney's office wants to proceed could be determined ahead of Monday's hearing, during it or even days after, she said.
"The three charges of first-degree murder are still pending; they are still hanging over Lindsay Clancy's head unless and until the DA announces otherwise," Hershon said.
Historically, Cruz, the district attorney, has made comments and announcements about the case at press conferences after court finishes. That could happen again this week, she predicted.
It is also likely, Hershon said, that Judge Sullivan pushes the lawyers on both sides to get a trial date on the calendar during Monday's hearing.
"It does not mean it's definitely going to be a jury trial, but [they will want to] put something in the books, hold those dates. It's a big chunk of time. It's four, five, six weeks of the court calendar; that's hard to fit in at the last minute," she said.
"I would anticipate they block off the time while they go through all these motions and the DA's office figures out what it wants to do."

title: Attempted murder probe after petrol bomb thrown at French riot police
content_c:
French officials have opened an investigation into the attempted murder of a police officer and Germany’s interior minister has called for harsh penalties after peaceful and mainly youth-led protests across Europe ended in violence.
In Portugal, police – some with dogs – cleared protest camps with baton charges, while security forces in Switzerland were attacked with paving stones.
Protests over the education system, deteriorating public services, declining prospects, unaffordable housing and the spiralling cost of living have shaken a number of countries this autumn.
Violence erupted in the French capital as well as Marseille, Grenoble, Bordeaux, Lyon and Toulouse on Saturday night after an estimated 320,000 demonstrators, some in Halloween costumes, took to the streets.
As the rallies ended, masked and hooded rioters arrived and caused what the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, described as an “extraordinary” level of violence. More than 770 people were arrested.
In Paris, the prosecutor’s office said incendiary devices were thrown at a group of about 15 gendarmes and police officers and a formal investigation had been opened for “attempted murder of persons vested with public authority”.
Injuries reportedly included second-degree burns in an incident captured on mobile phone video and shared on social media and broadcast on French television.
The level of physical violence and looting was significantly lower than on 17 October, when 2,600 people were arrested and as many as 3,000 shops pillaged in one of the worst nights of urban unrest in France’s recent history.
In Germany, looters and rioters rampaged through Frankfurt, the country’s financial hub, damaging stores and injuring more than 100 police officers.
“The rioters and looters will be identified and held accountable,” said Alexander Dobrindt, the hardline interior minister. He singled out “violent leftwing groups and troublemakers from the migrant community”, adding: “Tough penalties must follow this breach of the peace.”
Dobrindt told the tabloid newspaper Bild that deploying a heavy police presence across multiple locations had been effective. “Excesses of violence like those in Paris were prevented thanks to our highly committed police forces,” he said.
More than 100,000 protesters marched in over 30 German cities on Saturday to demand better education and lower living costs in protests led by the “Gen Z regelt” (Gen Z will sort it) campaign.
Hooded rioters damaged 17 Frankfurt shops, looting five of them, and threw missiles including petrol bombs, according to Roman Poseck, the state interior minister for Hesse.
More than 100 of the 1,300 police officers deployed in the city were injured and 54 suspects, aged from 13 to 29, were arrested. “I am shocked by what I have seen, and there is no point in sugar-coating it. Let me make this very clear: things cannot go on like this,” Poseck said.
Most of those arrested were German nationals, the minister said, adding that police estimated they had been confronted with “between 1,000 and 1,500 violent troublemakers, predominantly from a migrant background”.
Violence also broke out Saturday night in Cologne, where police used water cannon to disperse the crowd, and in Berlin, where protesters attacked police with bottles and fireworks. Gen Z regelt posted a statement distancing itself from all violence.
In Portugal, riot police removed protesters by force from Rossio Square in Lisbon at about 4.30am on Sunday after thousands of people angry at the housing crisis marched through the city on Saturday and set up camp.
The protesters want Portugal’s minority centre-right government to withdraw a bill that makes evictions easier and ends rent caps on new leases. A smaller camp in Porto was also cleared by force.
In Albania, masked protesters hurled stones and firebombs at police in the capital, Tirana, on the margins of a demonstration demanding the resignation of the prime minister, Edi Rama, over perceived corruption.
Youths threw paving stones and firebombs at police and set fire to rubbish bins at the end of a largely peaceful protest. The interior ministry said on Friday that 350 people had been hurt in the protests, including 200 police, with 269 minors arrested.
In Switzerland, hundreds of protesters gathered in Zürich and Basel on Saturday night for unauthorised demonstrations – both of which ended in violence – under the slogan: “We’ve had enough in Switzerland, too.”
In Zürich, police used water cannon, teargas and rubber bullets to disperse rioters attacking them with fireworks, bottles and stones, Swiss media reported. A police patrol car was damaged and rubbish bins and electric bikes set on fire.
In Basel, police said about 150 people gathered in the city centre at around 9pm. Shop windows were smashed, facades tagged with graffiti and bins and bikes set on fire, with incidents also reported in Geneva.

title: India news: Opposition holds major rally in Delhi over voter roll revisions
content_c:
India opposition holds major rally against voter roll revisions
Published November 1, 2026last updated November 1, 2026
What you need to know
This blog is closed. Here is our coverage from India on Sunday, November 1:
- India's opposition parties are marching to Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi to seek the resignation of the election chief over alleged voter roll manipulation
- Rahul Gandhi tells protesters that India's election chief 'will go to jail'
- Pollution curbs have kicked-in in the Indian capital
Thank you for reading!
That's all for today. We will be back with more news from India tomorrow.
Rahul Gandhi says India's election chief 'will go to jail'
Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would be removed from office and jailed, accusing him of facilitating electoral fraud.
Speaking at a rally organized by the opposition INDIA alliance in New Delhi, Gandhi alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah owed their positions to Kumar.
"Gyanesh Kumar will be removed from the post of Chief Election Commissioner. Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail," Gandhi told supporters.
The Congress leader also accused authorities of manipulating elections through electronic voting machines and changes to electoral rolls.
"For years, vote theft has been happening in this country," Gandhi said, citing several state elections and the 2024 parliamentary vote.
He further claimed that 15% of India's voters had been removed from electoral rolls following the 2024 election. The allegations have not been independently verified.
Gandhi also criticized economic inequality and the treatment of farmers, young people and workers.
"The farmer is not getting his rights. The youth are not getting employment. The laborer is not getting his rights, and the entire wealth has gone into the hands of two or three people," he said.
Home Minister Amit Shah denounces opposition rally
Union Home Minister Amit Shah took aim at opposition leader Rahul Gandhi from an event in Punjab state's Chandigarh on Sunday as the opposition alliance reached Ramlila Maidan for its rally.
He slammed the Congress for calling the opposition rally on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, which Shah said were "incited" by the main opposition party,
"Our party held a press conference requesting that they not hold the event on November 1, 2, 3 — the very days the anti-Sikh riots took place — as it would deeply hurt the sentiments of the Sikh community, including mothers, sisters, and children. But they remained adamant," Shah said.
The senior minister of the Modi government highlighted that he was speaking from Punjab, which he went on to say was the "land of the (Sikh) Gurus."
"I strongly condemn this vile attempt. India and Punjab will never be able to forget this," he said, referring to the opposition rally.
Congress and the opposition have accused Shah and Modi of "vote theft" amid allegations of electoral irregularities.
On Saturday, Shah challenged Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to discuss the "vote theft" row in a special session of the parliament. He has accused the opposition of evading parliamentary debate and making baseless allegations against India's poll body.
INDIA bloc leaders arrive at Ramlila Maidan
India's opposition leaders, led by Congress' Rahul Gandhi, have reached Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi — the ground-zero of their rally against a sweeping review of voter lists and their demand for the resignation of the chief election commissioner.
The rally is November's first public display of dissent, following near-daily protests in October by opposition parties, India's 'Cockroach' movement, student organizations and civil society groups over the Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls in the world's largest democracy.
Gandhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's political arch-rival, rode through an almost 1.5 kilometer-long (0.9 mile-long) stretch in New Delhi in an open-top jeep, with leaders of India's opposition parties seated behind him.
Thousands of people, including supporters and cadres of the opposition from different states, began gathering at Ramlila Maidan from Sunday morning, waving the national flag and party flags as they awaited the arrival of the opposition convoy.
Visuals on Indian news channels showed the opposition leaders taking their seats on a stage set up at the historic square.
Gandhi is expected to address the rally shortly.
Opposition leaders set off for Ramlila Maidan
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has shared visuals of the opposition INDIA alliance's rally headed toward Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.
A split screen showed a large crowd of supporters gathered at the rally site as promient opposition lawmakers seated onboard an open-top vehicle made their way to the Ramlila Maidan through Delhi's roads.
"Come to Connaught Place, let's march together. Or meet directly at Ramlila Maidan - but you must come," Gandhi wrote on X earlier at noon local time as he called for the march to "Save the Vote, Save the Nation."
Delhi enforces winter pollution plan
With winter on the horizon in New Delhi, dread of the annual smog that season brings with it has also set in.
Starting today, the Indian capital is imposing strict and sweeping pollution curbs to tackle the toxic winter smog.
The restrictions include a ban on older vehicles registered outside the city, a suspension of dust-generating demolition activities and outdoor civil construction activities, doubling of parking fees to discourage the use of private vehicles and reduction of physical attendance in government and private-sector offices to 50%.
Agencies including the Delhi Pollution Control Committee, the Municipal Corporation, the city's transport department and traffic police have been tasked with ensuring a stringent enforcement of the winter pollution rules.
The measures will be implemeted for varying time frames, with some lasting until February 28.
"Delhi's Winter Action Plan 2026-27 comes into effect with stricter pollution controls, stronger enforcement and 24×7 monitoring. We humbly request all Delhiites to follow the guidelines and contribute towards making Delhi's air cleaner and healthier," Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta's office said.
How has Modi's BJP reacted to the opposition stir?
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of Prime Minister Narendra Modi is staging a rally of its own in New Delhi, setting the stage for a battle of marches.
The BJP march will take place in West Delhi in remembrance of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, with the ruling party accusing the Congress of staging a political rally on the anniversary of the violence.
The deadly riots took place following the assassination of the then prime minister, Congress'Indira Gandhi— opposition leader Rahul Gandhi's paternal grandmother — by two Sikh bodyguards on October 31, 1984.
"The sobs of the 1984 riot victims cannot be drowned out by the noise of rallies!" the BJP wrote on X.
"The wounds of 1984 are still raw today. Congress cannot bury them under the din of its theatrics!" the party added.
The BJP also shared videos from different states in the country of rallies held over the weekend under its campaign named "Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy" to counter the Congress and the opposition.
The BJP deems the opposition protests over alleged voter roll manipulations as attempts to "create anarchy."
INDIA bloc holds big rally against electoral irregularities, election chief
India's political opposition is carrying out a major march in New Delhi to protest the nationwide revision of electoral rolls that they say benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
They are also seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The 'Chalo Dilli' march, heralded by the main opposition Congress party, will begin from Central Delhi's Connaught Place Minto Road Junction to reach Ramlila Maidan.
Top faces of the opposition alliance — called the INDIA bloc — are among those expected to participate. These include Congress' Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, Samajwadi Party supremo Akhilesh Yadav and Rashtriya Janata Dal's Tejashwi Yadav.
India's youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which carried out its own demonstrations against Kumar last month, has also backed the opposition rally.

Under a contentious nationwide voter-verification exercise, called the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), around 130 million names have been purged from electoral rolls.
The opposition and critics say that those struck off the voter lists include a large number of minority voters and accuse Modi's BJP of using the exercise as a tool to secure future electoral gains. BJP denied the allegations.
The outcry against election chief Kumar began in September after an investigative report by an Indian daily said that there were divisions in the country's poll body — the Election Commission of India (ECI) — over the revision of voter lists, which it oversees.
Concerns emerged over the ECI's independence.
The ECI has maintained the SIR removes deceased, relocated and duplicate voters and helps prevent the inclusion of "foreign illegal immigrants."

On Saturday evening, the INDIA bloc staged a mock impeachment of the chief election commissioner. The symbolic proceedings saw opposition members reenacting a parliamentary session in a garden at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence.
"I don't think anything like this has ever happened in history. The entire opposition sitting in a garden to discuss the impeachment of the CEC, it is absurd," leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi said.
He added that the opposition lawmakers had to hold the mock exercise — which even featured furniture, seating arrangements and carpeting resembling the Lok Sabha (lower house of the Indian parliament) — because they "have nowhere else to go."
"We have no other option. Every single institution ... is closed for us," Gandhi said.
Meanwhile on Sunday, the opposition expects thousands of supporters to descend upon Ramlila Maidan.
It is the first major demonstration to be held at the famous ground, located between Old and New Delhi, since it was labeled as one of the three designated protest sites in the capital last month.
Early visuals showed supporters beginning to gather at Ramlila Maidan and posters of the 'Chalo Dilli' march propped up in the capital.
The Delhi Police said that around 200 to 250 CCTV cameras have been set up at the site as part of the security arrangements.
News agency ANI reported that around 4,000 security personnel have been deployed at Ramlila Maidan.
"The organizers have set up various enclosures, and we have police personnel stationed within them. There are also pathways between these enclosures, where our police personnel are deployed to ensure the area remains secure,” deputy commissioner of police (Central District) Rohit Rajbir Singh told ANI.
The capital's traffic police announced curbs and diversions in Central Delhi ahead of the rally.
Welcome to our coverage
This is Dharvi Vaid Dhulia from DW’s studio in New Delhi, bringing you our daily capsule of all the biggest headlines making a splash in India.
New Delhi has been waking up to chillier mornings, but the political heat brought on by a weekend of protests by India's bloc of opposition parties is what's gripping the capital today.
The opposition is set to hold a massive rally today at Ramlila Maidan — New Delhi's newly designated protest site — against alleged voter roll irregularities and India's top poll official.
Last evening, the opposition parties staged a mock impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as they stepped up their stir against a controversial nationwide revision of voter lists.
In other news, pollution curbs to tackle the annual winter smog in the Indian capital have come into force.
Stay with us as we bring you all this and more.

title: USA: Privatjet stürzt in Wohngebiet in Florida – neun Tote
content_c:
Flugsicherheit in den USA Privatjet zerschellt in Wohngebiet in Florida – neun Tote
Beim Absturz eines Privatflugzeugs im US-Bundesstaat Florida sind Verkehrsminister Sean Duffy zufolge alle neun Insassen ums Leben gekommen. Die Maschine sei am Mittag (US-Ostküstenzeit) über einem Wohngebiet abgestürzt, teilte er auf der Plattform X mit.
Today's plane crash in Palm Beach County, Florida is a horrific tragedy
Here's what we know:
- At 12:50 PM ET, a Learjet 60 crashed in a neighborhood near Cresthaven, FL
- All 9 people on board were killed
- The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas…
Ich bin damit einverstanden, dass mir externe Inhalte angezeigt werden. Damit können personenbezogene Daten an Drittplattformen übermittelt werden. Mehr dazu in unserer Datenschutzerklärung.
Warum die Maschine verunglückte, blieb zunächst unklar. Auf dem Asphalt der Straße am Absturzort entstand ein riesiger Krater. Duffy sprach von einer »furchtbaren Tragödie«. Das Unglück ereignete sich um 12.50 Uhr Ortszeit (18.50 MEZ) in Greenacres.
Die Behörden kündigten Ermittlungen zur Unglücksursache ein. Laut US-Medien befand sich der Jet in einer Höhe von rund 11.000 Metern, als die Piloten Turbulenzen und Vereisungen meldeten. Kurz darauf geriet der Jet in Sturzflug und kam es zu der Katastrophe, die von zahlreichen Überwachungskameras gefilmt wurde.
Gewaltiger Krater in der Straße
Ob am Boden weitere Personen durch den Absturz verletzt oder getötet wurden, sagte Duffy zunächst nicht. Die Unglücksstelle liegt unmittelbar an einer viel befahrenen Straße und extrem nah an Wohnhäusern.
Szene von der Unglücksstelle
Foto: Eduin Cruz / REUTERS
Gouverneur Ron DeSantis sprach von einem verheerenden Flugzeugabsturz: »Es sah aus, wie eine Rakete, die einschlägt und hat einen großen Krater an der Straße hinterlassen.« Videoaufnahmen belegen dies. Zum Zeitpunkt des Unglücks herrschte in der Region extrem schlechtes Wetter.
Der Absturzort an der Ostküste der USA liegt nicht weit entfernt von der Privatresidenz Mar-a-Lago von Präsident Donald Trump. Im Endspurt vor den Parlamentswahlen am Dienstag hatte der Präsident Wahlkampftermine in anderen Bundesstaaten.

title: Polizei zieht Bilanz zu Krawallen in Frankfurt
content_c:
Polizei zu Krawallen Viele Randalierer in Frankfurt wohl ohne politisches Motiv
54 Festnahmen, zahlreiche Verletzte und fünf geplünderte Geschäfte: Nach den Krawallen in Frankfurt am Main hat die Polizei eine erste Bilanz gezogen. Bei einem überwiegenden Teil der Randalierer sei kein politisches Motiv erkennbar.
54 Festnahmen, 100 verletzte Polizisten, fünf geplünderte Geschäfte: Nach den schweren Ausschreitungen in Frankfurt haben Polizei und Innenministerium am Sonntag eine erste Bilanz gezogen. Demnach wurden 87 Strafanzeigen aufgenommen, 1.225 Platzverweise ausgesprochen und 366 Personen kontrolliert. Auch Feuerwehr und Rettungskräfte wurden angegriffen.
Nach den größtenteils friedlichen Gen-Z-Protesten war es am Samstagabend in der Frankfurter Innenstadt zu Plünderungen und massiver Gewalt gegen Einsatzkräfte gekommen. Die Ausschreitungen zogen sich bis tief in die Nacht. Bei einer Pressekonferenz am Sonntagmittag informierten Innenminister Roman Poseck (CDU), Polizeipräsident Stefan Müller, Einsatzleiter Erik Hessenmüller sowie Vertreter der Stadt Frankfurt über die bisherigen Erkenntnisse.
Polizei unterscheidet zwischen zwei Tätergruppen
Nach Einschätzung der Polizei muss hier zwischen unterschiedlichen Gruppen unterschieden werden. Gegen Ende der Demonstration sei eine kleinere Gruppe gewalttätig geworden, sagte Einsatzleiter Erik Hessenmüller. Die späteren Ausschreitungen auf der Zeil und in der übrigen Innenstadt schreibt die Polizei dagegen einer anderen Personengruppe zu.
Es sei eine schwierige Gemengelage für die Einsatzkräfte gewesen, sagte Hessenmüller. Bei der Aufarbeitung müsse deshalb genau differenziert werden, wer wann an den Ausschreitungen beteiligt gewesen sei.
Junge Männer ohne erkennbares politisches Motiv
Bei den nächtlichen Randalen und Plünderungen handelte es sich nach Einschätzung der Polizei vor allem um junge Männer mit Migrationshintergrund. Die Gruppen, die sich regelmäßig an Wochenenden in der Frankfurter Innenstadt treffen, seien der Polizei bereits bekannt, sagte Polizeipräsident Stefan Müller.
Bislang habe man diese Personen eher als "erlebnisorientiert" eingeordnet. Die Ereignisse vom Samstag hätten nun gezeigt, dass sie auch gewaltbereit seien. Ein politisches Motiv sei bei ihnen allerdings nicht erkennbar.
Die Polizei hofft, anhand der Videoaufnahmen weitere Tatverdächtige identifizieren zu können. Bei den bereits Festgenommenen handelt es sich um Menschen im Alter zwischen 13 und 29 Jahren. Nach Angaben von Innenminister Poseck besitzen sie überwiegend die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit.
Unter den Festgenommenen seien sowohl Frankfurter als auch Personen aus anderen Teilen Hessens und aus Nordrhein-Westfalen, sagte Müller.
Möglicherweise hätten sich einige der Randalierer die Bilder von Plünderungen in Frankreich zum Vorbild genommen. Welche Geschäfte angegriffen wurden, sei dabei offenbar eher zufällig gewesen.
Insgesamt wurden nach Polizeiangaben fünf Geschäfte geplündert. Angegriffen wurde auch ein Waffengeschäft. Dort konnte die Polizei mehrere Personen festnehmen und Schreckschusswaffen sicherstellen.
Bis zu 30 Einsatzorte gleichzeitig
Wie schwierig die Lage für die Einsatzkräfte war, verdeutlichten die Verantwortlichen anhand des Ausmaßes der Ausschreitungen. Zeitweise habe es bis zu 30 Einsatzorte gleichzeitig gegeben
Das große Gebiet mit seinen zahlreichen Straßen, kleinen Gassen und Innenhöfen habe den Polizeieinsatz erheblich erschwert. Hinzu sei die große Zahl an Randalierern gekommen.
Nach Angaben der Polizei wurden Einsatzkräfte mit Böllern und Molotowcocktails angegriffen, teilweise aus dem Hinterhalt. Außerdem errichteten Randalierer Barrikaden.
Poseck spricht von "entsetzlichem Gewaltexzess"
Poseck bezeichnete die Ausschreitungen als "entsetzlichen Gewaltexzess". Für die Einsatzkräfte sei es eine außerordentlich schwierige Nacht gewesen.
Nach seinen Angaben wurden 100 Polizisten verletzt, einer davon schwer. Der Beamte habe einen Stein ins Gesicht bekommen. Das seien "Bilder, die nicht in unser Stadtbild gehören", sagte Poseck.
Die Gruppe von schätzungsweise 1.000 bis 1.500 Störern sei überwiegend "migrantisch geprägt" gewesen, sagte er. Zugleich sagte er, dass die Festgenommenen mehrheitlich deutsche Staatsangehörige seien.
Es dürfe nun "keine falschen Tabus geben", forderte Poseck. Er setze "auf Inhaftierungen und abschreckende Strafen".
Innenminister kündigt härtere Gangart an
Für Poseck sind die Ausschreitungen eine "Initialzündung für eine härtere Gangart". Die Nacht müsse klare Konsequenzen haben. Die Täter müssten die "ganze Härte des Rechtsstaates" spüren.
Der Innenminister kündigte an, stärker gegen Strukturen von "gewaltbereiten Menschen mit Migrationshintergrund" vorgehen zu wollen. Ziel sei es, mögliche Gefahren frühzeitig zu erkennen.
Auch Ministerpräsident Boris Rhein (CDU) zeigte sich schockiert von den Gewaltexzessen. Diese würden nicht ohne Konsequenzen bleiben, sagte er der Deutschen Presse-Agentur.
"Wer sich so verhält wie die Angreifer in der Frankfurter Innenstadt, stellt sich außerhalb unserer Gesellschaft. Wir werden Aggressoren, Tätergruppen und Hergang genau bewerten und unsere Schlüsse ziehen."
Oberbürgermeister Josef: "Mir ist völlig egal, welchen Pass jemand hat"
Frankfurts Oberbürgermeister Mike Josef (SPD) zeigte sich ebenfalls erschüttert. Er sei "fassungslos und wütend", sagte er auf der Pressekonferenz. "Es tut mir weh, unsere Stadt so zu sehen."
Anders als Innenminister Poseck stellte Josef dabei nicht die Herkunft der mutmaßlichen Täter in den Mittelpunkt. "Mir ist völlig egal, welchen Pass jemand hat oder wo seine Eltern geboren sind", sagte der Oberbürgermeister. Wer Gewalt ausübe, müsse die juristischen Konsequenzen tragen.
"Gen Z regelt" distanziert sich von Gewalt
Die Organisatoren der Gen-Z-Demonstration distanzierten sich ausdrücklich von den Ausschreitungen. "Was nach dem Ende der Kundgebungen passiert ist, darauf hatten wir keinen Einfluss", erklärte ein Sprecher der Initiative "Gen Z regelt".
Bereits am Samstagabend hatte die Initiative auf Instagram eine Stellungnahme veröffentlicht. Darin distanzierte sie sich von "jeglicher Form der Gewalt sowie von gewalttätigen Handlungen anderer Gruppen oder Einzelpersonen", die nicht Teil der Demonstrationen gewesen seien.
"Wir stehen für friedlichen Protest, demokratische Werte und das Recht, unsere Meinung frei zu äußern. Gewalt war und ist niemals Teil unserer Bewegung."
Trotz der Ausschreitungen will die Initiative weiter demonstrieren. Die Proteste am Samstag seien nur ein erster Schritt gewesen. In drei Wochen sollen erneut bundesweit Menschen mobilisiert werden.
"Wir wollen uns an den europaweiten Protesten am 20. November beteiligen", sagte ein Sprecher des Presseteams, der öffentlich nur unter seinem Vornamen Amadeo auftreten möchte, der Deutschen Presse-Agentur.
description: 54 Festnahmen, zahlreiche Verletzte und fünf geplünderte Geschäfte: Nach den Krawallen in Frankfurt am Main hat die Polizei eine erste Bilanz gezogen. Bei einem überwiegenden Teil der Randalierer sei kein politisches Motiv erkennbar.
author: tagesschau.de
content:
Polizei zu Krawallen Viele Randalierer in Frankfurt wohl ohne politisches Motiv
54 Festnahmen, zahlreiche Verletzte und fünf geplünderte Geschäfte: Nach den Krawallen in Frankfurt am Main hat die Polizei eine erste Bilanz gezogen. Bei einem überwiegenden Teil der Randalierer sei kein politisches Motiv erkennbar.
54 Festnahmen, 100 verletzte Polizisten, fünf geplünderte Geschäfte: Nach den schweren Ausschreitungen in Frankfurt haben Polizei und Innenministerium am Sonntag eine erste Bilanz gezogen. Demnach wurden 87 Strafanzeigen aufgenommen, 1.225 Platzverweise ausgesprochen und 366 Personen kontrolliert. Auch Feuerwehr und Rettungskräfte wurden angegriffen.
Nach den größtenteils friedlichen Gen-Z-Protesten war es am Samstagabend in der Frankfurter Innenstadt zu Plünderungen und massiver Gewalt gegen Einsatzkräfte gekommen. Die Ausschreitungen zogen sich bis tief in die Nacht. Bei einer Pressekonferenz am Sonntagmittag informierten Innenminister Roman Poseck (CDU), Polizeipräsident Stefan Müller, Einsatzleiter Erik Hessenmüller sowie Vertreter der Stadt Frankfurt über die bisherigen Erkenntnisse.
Polizei unterscheidet zwischen zwei Tätergruppen
Nach Einschätzung der Polizei muss hier zwischen unterschiedlichen Gruppen unterschieden werden. Gegen Ende der Demonstration sei eine kleinere Gruppe gewalttätig geworden, sagte Einsatzleiter Erik Hessenmüller. Die späteren Ausschreitungen auf der Zeil und in der übrigen Innenstadt schreibt die Polizei dagegen einer anderen Personengruppe zu.
Es sei eine schwierige Gemengelage für die Einsatzkräfte gewesen, sagte Hessenmüller. Bei der Aufarbeitung müsse deshalb genau differenziert werden, wer wann an den Ausschreitungen beteiligt gewesen sei.
Junge Männer ohne erkennbares politisches Motiv
Bei den nächtlichen Randalen und Plünderungen handelte es sich nach Einschätzung der Polizei vor allem um junge Männer mit Migrationshintergrund. Die Gruppen, die sich regelmäßig an Wochenenden in der Frankfurter Innenstadt treffen, seien der Polizei bereits bekannt, sagte Polizeipräsident Stefan Müller.
Bislang habe man diese Personen eher als "erlebnisorientiert" eingeordnet. Die Ereignisse vom Samstag hätten nun gezeigt, dass sie auch gewaltbereit seien. Ein politisches Motiv sei bei ihnen allerdings nicht erkennbar.
Die Polizei hofft, anhand der Videoaufnahmen weitere Tatverdächtige identifizieren zu können. Bei den bereits Festgenommenen handelt es sich um Menschen im Alter zwischen 13 und 29 Jahren. Nach Angaben von Innenminister Poseck besitzen sie überwiegend die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit.
Unter den Festgenommenen seien sowohl Frankfurter als auch Personen aus anderen Teilen Hessens und aus Nordrhein-Westfalen, sagte Müller.
Möglicherweise hätten sich einige der Randalierer die Bilder von Plünderungen in Frankreich zum Vorbild genommen. Welche Geschäfte angegriffen wurden, sei dabei offenbar eher zufällig gewesen.
Insgesamt wurden nach Polizeiangaben fünf Geschäfte geplündert. Angegriffen wurde auch ein Waffengeschäft. Dort konnte die Polizei mehrere Personen festnehmen und Schreckschusswaffen sicherstellen.
Bis zu 30 Einsatzorte gleichzeitig
Wie schwierig die Lage für die Einsatzkräfte war, verdeutlichten die Verantwortlichen anhand des Ausmaßes der Ausschreitungen. Zeitweise habe es bis zu 30 Einsatzorte gleichzeitig gegeben
Das große Gebiet mit seinen zahlreichen Straßen, kleinen Gassen und Innenhöfen habe den Polizeieinsatz erheblich erschwert. Hinzu sei die große Zahl an Randalierern gekommen.

title: У Болгарії проросійська Йотова перемагає на виборах президента: які результати
content_c:
У Болгарії проросійська Йотова перемагає на виборах президента: які результати
Після опрацювання понад 92% протоколів Іліяна Йотова випереджає проукраїнського кандидата Андрея Гюрова майже на 18 відсоткових пунктів.
На президентських виборах у Болгарії за попередніми результатами перемагає проросійська кандидатка Іліяна Йотова. Її суперник, прозахідний і проукраїнський політик Андрей Гюров, посідає друге місце.
Про це повідомляє БНТ із посиланням на дані Центральної виборчої комісії Болгарії.
Станом на 02:00 після опрацювання 92,39% протоколів Йотова та кандидат у віцепрезиденти Кирил Вилчев отримали 57,36% голосів. За Гюрова та його партнера Георгія Кандева проголосували 39,68% виборців.
Варіант «Не підтримую нікого» обрали 2,96% учасників голосування. Другий тур виборів відбувся 1 листопада.
Йотова, яка наразі виконує президентські обов’язки, є соратницею прем’єра Румена Радева. Як пояснювала «Європейська правда», вона асоціюється з його політичною силою «Прогресивна Болгарія» та її курсом щодо України й західних партнерів.
Її опонент Гюров представляє євроатлантичну та проукраїнську опозицію за підтримки коаліції «Продовжуємо зміни — Демократична Болгарія». Навесні, коли він виконував обов’язки прем’єра, Болгарія підписала безпекову угоду з Україною.
Програма Гюрова передбачає тіснішу співпрацю з партнерами в ЄС і НАТО та активнішу протидію російській загрозі.
Нагадаємо, що раніше прем’єр Болгарії зробив несподівану заяву про домовленості Трампа й Путіна

title: Нетаньяху призывает Трампа нанести удар по Ирану сразу после выборов в США — Axios
content_c:
Премьер-министр Израиля Биньямин Нетаньяху призывает президента США Дональда Трампа нанести удар по Ирану сразу после промежуточных выборов в США. Трамп пока хочет дать шанс переговорам, что вызывает беспокойство у израильского премьера. Об этом сообщило издание Axios.
Президент США Дональд Трамп в субботу провел откровенный телефонный разговор с премьер-министром Израиля Биньямином Нетаньяху. Они обсудили ход американских переговоров с Ираном и то, как быстро следует возобновить боевые действия. Об этом рассказали один израильский и один американский источник издания.
По их словам, Нетаньяху оказывает давление на Трампа, добиваясь нанесения ударов по Ирану сразу после промежуточных выборов в США во вторник. Однако американский президент пока хочет дождаться результатов переговоров. Такой подход беспокоит израильского премьера. Израильский источник назвал разговор «жестким», тогда как американский охарактеризовал его как «прямой».
Как и перед операцией Midnight Hammer в июне 2025 года и операцией Epic Fury в феврале, Трамп одновременно действует в двух направлениях. Он пытается достичь договоренности о возобновлении мирных переговоров. Параллельно продолжается подготовка к возможному возобновлению масштабных боевых действий после промежуточных выборов.
На прошлой неделе вице-президент США Джей Ди Венс направил письмо иранскому руководителю по вопросам национальной безопасности Мохсену Резаи. Речь шла о возможности возобновления переговоров. Это стало обращением Вашингтона к Тегерану на самом высоком уровне за последние несколько месяцев.
В субботу Трамп заявил журналистам, что переговоры с Ираном «идут хорошо». Он также подчеркнул, что «не очень торопится». По словам американского президента, иранская сторона хочет заключить соглашение, однако он считает его ненадежным. «Они заключают соглашение, а потом отказываются от него», — сказал Трамп. В то же время президент заявил, что Соединенным Штатам еще нужно «разобраться» с одним или двумя ядерными объектами в Иране.
«Мы можем сделать это за десять минут. Мы это спланировали. Посмотрите на Pickaxe Mountain. С этим нужно разобраться. Мы можем сделать это очень быстро», — заявил Трамп.
Он имел в виду вероятный ядерный объект, обустроенный внутри горы. В воскресенье катарские посредники третий день подряд встречались с иранскими чиновниками. Они пытались достичь договоренности, которая позволит возобновить прямые переговоры между США и Ираном.
Министр иностранных дел Ирана Аббас Арагчи в воскресенье заявил, что соглашения пока нет. Он подчеркнул, что его достижение зависит от ответов Соединенных Штатов на вопросы Ирана.
«Мы прилагаем все усилия в этом направлении и надеемся, что другая сторона проявит достаточно здравого смысла, чтобы выбрать дипломатию вместо других путей», — сказал Арагчи.
Напомним, что перед израильскими выборами премьер-министр Биньямин Нетаньяху, по сообщениям, пытался убедить Дональда Трампа возобновить удары по Ирану. Также появилась информация о его конфликте с начальником Генштаба Эялем Замиром из-за приказа, который мог спровоцировать столкновение с Тегераном. Нетаньяху опроверг сообщения о конфликте, а Минобороны Израиля опровергло намерения проводить операции против Ирана.
Кроме того, по данным источников, США предупредили несколько стран Персидского залива о возможной новой кампании против Ирана после промежуточных выборов. Вашингтон направлял в Израиль дополнительную систему Patriot и выводил военных с уязвимых баз на Ближнем Востоке. Чиновники также сообщали о пополнении запасов боеприпасов и подготовке бомбардировщиков и истребителей к нанесению ударов. Окончательного решения Трамп на тот момент не принял, а альтернативой оставалась попытка заключить соглашение.

По словам американского президента, иранская сторона хочет заключить соглашение, однако он считает его ненадежным. «Они заключают соглашение, а потом отказываются от него», — сказал Трамп. В то же время президент заявил, что Соединенным Штатам еще нужно «разобраться» с одним или двумя ядерными объектами в Иране.
«Мы можем сделать это за десять минут. Мы это спланировали. Посмотрите на Pickaxe Mountain. С этим нужно разобраться. Мы можем сделать это очень быстро», — заявил Трамп.
Он имел в виду вероятный ядерный объект, обустроенный внутри горы. В воскресенье катарские посредники третий день подряд встречались с иранскими чиновниками. Они пытались достичь договоренности, которая позволит возобновить прямые переговоры между США и Ираном.
Министр иностранных дел Ирана Аббас Арагчи в воскресенье заявил, что соглашения пока нет. Он подчеркнул, что его достижение зависит от ответов Соединенных Штатов на вопросы Ирана.
«Мы прилагаем все усилия в этом направлении и надеемся, что другая сторона проявит достаточно здравого смысла, чтобы выбрать дипломатию вместо других путей», — сказал Арагчи.
Напомним, что перед израильскими выборами премьер-министр Биньямин Нетаньяху, по сообщениям, пытался убедить Дональда Трампа возобновить удары по Ирану. Также появилась информация о его конфликте с начальником Генштаба Эялем Замиром из-за приказа, который мог спровоцировать столкновение с Тегераном. Нетаньяху опроверг сообщения о конфликте, а Минобороны Израиля опровергло намерения проводить операции против Ирана.
Кроме того, по данным источников, США предупредили несколько стран Персидского залива о возможной новой кампании против Ирана после промежуточных выборов. Вашингтон направлял в Израиль дополнительную систему Patriot и выводил военных с уязвимых баз на Ближнем Востоке. Чиновники также сообщали о пополнении запасов боеприпасов и подготовке бомбардировщиков и истребителей к нанесению ударов. Окончательного решения Трамп на тот момент не принял, а альтернативой оставалась попытка заключить соглашение.

title: Кількість постраждалих у Козятині на Вінниччині зросла до шістьох зокрема чотирьох дітей – поліція
content_c:
Кількість постраждалих унаслідок російського удару по території навчального закладу в Козятині Вінницької області зросла до шістьох осіб, серед яких четверо дітей, водночас жертвами атаки стали двоє людей, повідомила Патрульна поліція України у неділю.
"У Козятині ворог вдарив по території навчального закладу: двоє загиблих, шестеро постраждалих, серед них четверо дітей. Унаслідок атаки пошкоджено будівлі навчального закладу. Ми надавали домедичну допомогу травмованій жінці, однак, на жаль, попри зусилля медиків, вона померла в лікарні", – йдеться в повідомленні правоохоронців у телеграм-каналі.
За даними відомства, екіпажі патрульної поліції також доправили до медичного закладу двох травмованих дітей і забезпечили безперешкодний проїзд транспорту екстрених служб до місця влучання.
Як повідомлялося, у неділю російський безпілотник поцілив по території гуртожитку професійного училища в Козятині Вінницької області. Начальниця Вінницької обласної військової адміністрації (ОВА) Наталя Заболотна раніше інформувала про двох загиблих, однією з яких виявилася 13-річна дівчинка, та чотирьох поранених, зокрема двох п'ятирічних дівчаток, 16-річного юнака і 24-річного чоловіка.
Джерело: https://t.me/patrolpolice_ua/14896

title: Democrats are used to heartbreak in Texas - could Talarico turn the tide?
content_c:
Democrats are used to heartbreak in Texas - could Talarico turn the tide?
- Published
The race for a US Senate seat in Texas may prove crucial in determining which party controls Congress next year – a significant prize in its own right - but for both parties it represents so much more than that.
For the Democrats, their losing streak in statewide elections now stretches back more than three decades. In the second most populous state in America, liberals have been in the wilderness for a generation.
But polls suggest their candidate, 37-year-old James Talarico, may be on the verge of breaking through and turning a Texas Senate seat blue for the first time since 1988.
That would be a dream scenario for Democrats - and a potential nightmare for Republicans.
"If the Democrats do pull it off, I think it's going to cause a lot of soul searching and a lot of psychological damage to the Republican Party in Texas and nationwide," said Brendan Steinhauser, a Texas-based Republican campaign strategist.
These dramatic stakes help explain how this Senate race has rocketed to become the most expensive in US history, with total spending reaching more than half a billion dollars.
For Talarico, it has been a remarkable rise for a candidate who in 2025 was a relatively unknown state-level Democrat.
At the Fiesta Center in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday night, the line to see the softly spoken former teacher, who studied to be a Christian minister, stretched around the building and down the wide parking lot to a busy road.
In this dusty western plains town of about 250,000, which voted overwhelmingly for President Donald Trump two years ago, a visit from a major Democratic candidate on the eve of an election was unusual.
"It's just so amazing to watch," said Aaron Gonzalez, the Democratic Party chair for Hockley County, which borders Lubbock. "This time is different."
When Talarico took the stage before an estimated 3,000 supporters – with another thousand listening on speakers outside - his pitch was a familiar one for many national Democrats this year, albeit with a Texas twist.
He railed against a conservative political establishment that he said is insensitive to the economic hardship of average Americans. He condemned the corrosive influence of big money in politics. And he promised to advance a "comprehensive anti-corruption agenda" in the Senate.
"Texans are ready for change," he said. "We are done with the extremism and the corruption. We're done with the politics of division, and we are ready for something new."
The slogan for his final two weeks of campaigning – "clear eyes, full hearts, can't lose" – is taken from Friday Night Lights, a popular early 2000s TV show about a plucky small-town Texas high school football team.
His music playlist leans heavily on twangy Texas country music. He celebrates Texas breakfast tacos, quotes legendary Texas singer-songwriter Lyle Lovett and frequently mentions that his ties to the state go back eight generations.
In the Lubbock audience, Andrew Robinson, a student from nearby Texas Tech University, liked what he heard. But the 26-year-old's optimism was tempered by an entire lifetime spent watching Democrats try, and fail, to get a toehold in the state.
"A Talarico win would mean so much," he said. "I haven't been keen on wanting to stay in Texas. And if the government were to change, it could give me a reason."
For Republicans, a Democratic win in Texas would have a very different meaning.
At roughly the same time Talarico was addressing his supporters in the Fiesta Center, Trump – alongside the Republican Party's Senate candidate Ken Paxton – was just a few miles away, in a venue twice the size.
"If you go out and vote, we're going to have a tremendous win in Texas," the president told the crowd.
Trump's visit to reliably-Republican Lubbock suggests the party is concerned about turnout even in the most conservative portions of the state. It is a worry that has been echoed by other Texas Republicans.
"Understand, we could lose Texas," Texas Senator Ted Cruz said in his podcast on Friday. "The Democrats are massively out-turning-out the Republicans."
Don Huffines, who is running for election as the state's chief financial officer, issued an even more dire warning. "Texas is the foundation of the Republican Party in America," he posted on X.
"When the foundation breaks, it all falls apart. When we lose Texas, we lose the USA."
For weeks now, party leaders have been warning that a liberal breakthrough in the Lone Star State could have dire consequences.
They fear a Talarico win would motivate more local Democrats to run for statewide and federal offices. Better quality candidates with more funding could lead to a snowball effect similar to the Democratic inroads seen in other southern states, such as Georgia, North Carolina and Virginia.
"I think that it's pretty clear that Republicans, especially candidates, consultants, operatives, and others who are active in the party, see that this is a real threat," said Steinhauser.
"The days of waving this off and saying that Texas would never turn blue are over."
For the Texas Senate race to come to the point where recent polls suggest Talarico has a slim but stable lead has required a unique confluence of events and political dynamics – a "perfect storm", in the words of Steinhauser.
"Everything that could go well for the Democrats is going well," he said, "and everything that could go badly for the Republicans is going badly."
But it is also a whirlwind that, in a significant part, has been sown over the past year by Trump himself.
The national environment for Republicans is a harsh one.
Voters are frustrated with high consumer costs, including the price of petrol, and largely blame Trump's tariff policies and the Iran war.
Political corruption has become an issue of growing concern. Democrats, independents and many Republicans in a recent Cook political report poll identified "greedy billionaires and corporations" and politicians seeking "personal gain" as the ones to blame.
Texas-specific issues have also contributed to a hostile climate for the in-power party.
Polling and recent special elections in Texas indicate that Hispanic voters – many of whom switched to Trump to help him win the White House in 2024 – have soured on the administration's immigration enforcement policies.
Hispanics make up nearly a third of the state's population - and in more than a week of early voting in Texas, they have been casting ballots in historically large numbers.
Data centre construction, which Texas Republicans had touted as a welcome investment in the state, has drawn widespread criticism, particularly in rural areas that have traditionally been solidly conservative.
Texas Governor Greg Abbott, in his own tight re-election race, recently announced a one-year moratorium on AI construction in the state – a reflection of how quickly the issue has become a political liability.
"It's bad for Republicans," one Texas political strategist, who asked to remain anonymous, told the BBC. "We're asking a whole lot of the electorate at this point for us to continue to be the guys in charge."
Then there's the baggage that Paxton, who defeated longtime incumbent Senator John Cornyn in a contentious primary campaign earlier this year, brings to the race.
The 63-year-old Republican successfully painted the 74-year-old Cornyn as too old and too out-of-touch with Texas conservatives. He received a late boost, just days before his run-off election victory over Cornyn, in the form of a Trump endorsement.
"Ken Paxton has gone through a lot, in many cases, very unfairly, but he is a Fighter, and knows how to WIN," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Our Country needs Fighters, and also Loyalty to the Cause of Greatness."
The "a lot" the president referenced Paxton going through includes a 2015 federal indictment on charges of securities fraud – later dropped – and a 2023 impeachment by the Republican-controlled Texas House of Representatives on corruption, bribery and abuse of power charges.
The Texas Senate would later acquit Paxton after Trump intervened to pressure state Republican leaders.
All of this has meant that Paxton has more than a few critics – and enemies - in Texas, including within his own party.
Talarico, by contrast, has proven to be an effective candidate. The state legislator defeated a well-known opponent, Dallas Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett, in the Democratic primary.
Since earning the nomination, he has maintained his polling lead despite a withering onslaught of negative advertising - much of it funded by the world's richest man Elon Musk, whose SpaceX company is based in Texas.
Musk alone has funnelled more than $170m into the race. Trump's MAGA Inc. committee has chipped in $40m.
While Paxton has proven to be an ineffective fundraiser, the third-party money spent on his behalf has blanketed the airwaves in the state – spilling over into sporting events involving Texas teams that air across the nation.
They have targeted Talarico for his past comments supporting transgender people, for calling "radicalised white men" a domestic terrorism threat and for criticising the fossil fuel and beef industries – two powerful interests in the state.
Talarico has distanced himself from some of those earlier comments, arguing many were taken out of context and "missed the mark" or were "deliberately provocative" or "cringy".
Meanwhile, the Texas Democrat has proven to be a historically successful fundraiser, amassing more than $140m in donations over the course of his campaign and setting a three-month fundraising record for a Senate candidate.
The funding has allowed Talarico to hit back at Paxton, highlighting his past controversies, and defending himself from Republican attacks.
He frequently leans into his religious upbringing – as the grandson of a Southern Baptist preacher who spent time in a seminary – leavening his stump speeches with biblical references.
There is one particular passage Talarico has been partial to of late – the familiar Old Testament showdown between scrappy David and the giant Goliath.
"We are going up against our own Goliaths," he said in Lubbock. "The billionaire mega-donors, the corporate special interests, the entire Washington DC establishment. Their power is real, but so is ours."
But the power of Texas Democrats has been overestimated in the past. In 2018, Congressman Beto O'Rourke posted his own historic fundraising numbers, generated serious national attention and ultimately lost to Texas Senator Cruz by just over 2%.
Talarico's polling lead, while stable, continues to rest near the margin of error in most surveys. And last-minute Republican appeals, as well as Trump's repeated campaign visits, could spur conservatives to turn out in greater numbers on election day, erasing any Democratic early voting advantages.
Inside the tiny Democratic Party office at a Talarico rally in Amarillo on Tuesday, retired schoolteacher Terri Mills listened to the candidate's stump speech.
Despite acknowledging the decades of Democratic futility and false dawns, she said she was allowing herself to hope for a Democratic victory once again.
"I have gotten my hopes up before, you know," she said. "But I do feel that this time is a little different."
Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here. Those outside the UK can sign up here.

title: Negotiators ‘braced for worst’ over US-Iran talks to reopen strait of Hormuz
content_c:
Officials from the Gulf states are “braced for the worst” as they wait for Washington’s response to an Iranian proposal that could reopen the strait of Hormuz before the US midterm elections on Tuesday.
Indirect talks in Doha ran into a third day on Sunday with Qatar trying to negotiate the release of more than $6bn in Iranian assets, which could lead to the reopening of the strait of Hormuz and the restart of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.
The United Arab Emirates envoy Anwar Gargash said another round of escalation was not in the interests of Iran or any of its neighbours. He said: “We are also, as we have shown before, braced for the worst.”
He added: “Relations with Iran are essential, because Iran is our neighbour and we do not want to see it get caught up in a prolonged crisis.”
Qatar’s mediation continued despite unidentified missiles striking a Pakistan-bound Qatari LNG tanker near the strait of Hormuz on Friday. The attack came despite the ship receiving direct clearance and safe-passage approval from Tehran just hours earlier.
In a bid to overcome the lack of trust on both sides, Qatar has been focusing its efforts on reaching an agreement for a plan to compress the process by which the US lifts sanctions and then Iran reopens the strait of Hormuz and starts nuclear talks. Iran has agreed to cut the timetable from seven to two days.
Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said he hoped the US would choose “diplomacy over other paths”. He said Iran was ready for both defence and diplomacy, depending on Washington’s “rationality”. Araghchi said there were currently no plans for direct talks with Washington.
Araghchi has not been attending the mediation in Doha and is due to go to Turkmenistan on Monday, but other Iranian diplomats are heavily involved.
Donald Trump said on Saturday the US had knocked out much of Iran’s military but still had to “take care of” one or two targets, as Tehran warned of reprisals if attacked. He maintained that negotiations with Iran to end the war, started by the US and Israel in February, were “going fine but you know they’re not very reliable”.
Earlier on Saturday, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said the US was open to a diplomatic solution, while Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, disclosed that he had received a letter from the US vice-president, JD Vance, seeking to revive talks.
Rezaei noted what he described as a positive change in “tone” from the US side but said he had yet to respond.
Speaking to Al Jazeera on Saturday, Araghchi said Iran had offered to open the strait of Hormuz within two days of the US acting to lift the blockade on oil ships, stop blocking the release of Iranian assets and end sanctions on Iranian oil exports.
Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of Iran’s parliament, once again signalled that Tehran would be unwilling to discuss its nuclear programme, saying: “Our enemies must understand that the Iranian nation has made a decision not to negotiate on the nuclear issue under any circumstances or under any pressure. This great nation gave its enemies enough opportunity to negotiate in this area, but was faced with repeated breaches of promises and illegal bombing of part of peaceful nuclear facilities.”
Rezaei claimed Trump was being hounded by a war that he claimed was having wider international repercussions than the Vietnam war. He told Iranian TV on Saturday: “Today, wherever Trump goes, he must answer why he started the war against Iran. There is no family in America that has not endured the pressure caused by the war in Iran.”

title: Donald Trump loses allies after elections in Serbia and Brazil
content_c:
Donald Trump loses allies after elections in Serbia and Brazil
November 1, 2026
The midterm elections in the United States are just around the corner: On Tuesday, November 3, American voters will choose their representatives to the US Congress. The right-wing-conservative Republican party of President Donald Trump currently has a majority in both chambers.
But in other parts of the world election results are already in. The majority of voters in both Serbia and Brazil cast their ballots for left-wing parties. Those results will not influence the midterms in the US, but the victories of the Student List in Serbia and the incumbent president, Luiz Inacio "Lula" da Silva, in Brazil are bad news for Trump all the same.
In Serbia, he has lost an important European ally in outgoing president Aleksandar Vucic. And in Brazil, the Trump camp had been hoping Flavio Bolsonaro would triumph.
"Trump was a strong supporter of both Jair Bolsonaro, the Trump-like figure who served as president before Lula defeated him in 2022, and of his son Flavio," says Lawrence J. Haas, a senior fellow for US foreign policy at the American Foreign Policy Council, who was communications director for Al Gore, Bill Clinton's vice president, in the 1990s. "Trump wasn't happy about the defeat of either Bolsonaro," he continues, "and he doesn't feel warmly toward Lula. So relations will remain cool at best."
Trump declared Brazilian election looked "rigged"
Flavio Bolsonaro is under investigation in Brazil for alleged corruption and money laundering. After losing the election, he fled the country for Florida. The US State Department granted him and his family entry visas in spite of the pending legal action.
Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat. Instead, he claims there were irregularities in the vote. This is very reminiscent of Trump, who continues to claim – falsely – that Joe Biden and the Democratic Party "stole" the US election in 2020. Trump's comments on Bolsonaro's defeat sounded very familiar. "It looked like another rigged election, frankly," the US president said on Monday. "Elections have to be indisputable – and it looked very bad to me."
Good relations with Putin ally Vucic
Aleksandar Vucic had ruled Serbia as president with an iron fist since 2017. He resigned just before these elections in order to stand as prime minister, a role he previously held from 2014 to 2017. Vucic has commented in the past that he and President Trump are like-minded people. Trump's eldest son, Donald Jr., visited Vucic in Belgrade shortly before the US presidential elections in November 2024, and again a few months later.
The US Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC), which is closely connected with Trump's MAGA ("Make America Great Again") movement, recently announced that it was organizing a meeting in Belgrade in November, at which Vucic was to be a keynote speaker. It is unclear whether this is still the case.
Another thing Vucic and Trump have in common is that the soon-to-be-ex-president of Serbia has a much more positive attitude toward Russian president Vladimir Putin than do most other European heads of state. Vucic did not join EU countries in imposing sanctions on Russia after it launched its war of aggression against Ukraine. Belgrade still buys Russian raw materials, and Serbian state media under Vucic presented a more positive image of Russia than of the EU.
Trump also seems increasingly inclined toward Moscow. His special envoy Steve Witkoff recently described Putin as a "humanitarian," while, in an interview, Trump himself openly admitted that he got on better with Putin than with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The end of the Vucic government now means that Trump has lost one of his few allies in Europe who takes a similar view.
Israel: Outcome still unclear
There's still a chance of an outcome in the Israeli elections that might be to Trump's liking. With more than 96% of votes counted, the right-wing bloc led by prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu is in the lead. However, Trump ally Netanyahu has lost his majority, and the coalition negotiations will be very difficult.
Trump and Netanyahu have been close allies since well before February this year, when they joined forces to launch a war against Iran. In 2018, during his first term in office, Trump moved the US embassy in Israel from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem. This was controversial, because both Israel and Palestinians claim Jerusalem as their capital. Netanyahu's camp welcomed the decision.
Today, the United States is still by far Israel's most important partner, while Israel is an important regional ally for the US. It is not clear what their relationship would be like with a different Israeli government. If Netanyahu remains in power, little, if anything, will change.
No rosy prospects for Trump in the midterms
With Vucic's defeat, Trump has lost a loyal ally. And Lula's victory means, for him, that a disagreeable president remains in power. None of this is good for Trump, but foreign policy analyst Haas said it won't influence the important midterm elections in his country. "Americans will be voting [...] on the basis of issues that affect them, and how they feel about the party in power."
But this doesn't bode well for Trump, either. "Trump has the lowest approval rating of any president on the eve of a mid-term election since Harry Truman in 1946," Haas explained. "Americans are very concerned about issues of affordability, [and] they strongly oppose the US-Iran war."
Benjamin Alvarez Gruber in Miami contributed to this report, which was originally written in German.
description: Flavio Bolsonaro failed to gain power, Aleksandar Vucic was voted out of office, and even Benjamin Netanyahu's position has weakened. An unhappy US President Trump is crying electoral fraud.
